The safety assessment he had to submit before taking on the job had an exemption for riggers and scaffolders for wearing harnesses at all times outside a protected edge from the government authority.

I used to work for an Ag company that used a lot of pesticides and herbicides. There was a storm drain outside the bay door where the containment area was. More than once it appeared that "product" leaked so much that the containment filled up and seeped out under the door.

The trail always lead straight to the storm drain. I feel bad for mother nature.

This was a while back. I wish I had reported it at the time, but I was younger, dumber, needed the job and feared retaliation. They even had us pressure wash the evidence trail from the door to the drain a few times.

I was a Process Engineer working alarm rationalization. While talking to the operators on site I noticed their alarm panel was selectively covered with electrical tape. About a quarter of the alarm lights were covered and not visible. In addition the klaxon was covered with a piece of cardboard effectively reducing the db by half. Over the course of an hour long assessment three operators acknowledged 14 alarms. All of which were muted with barely any investigation. Several of the alarms were level one or very serious alarms. A dump of the last month of alarms showed that over 3000 alarm conditions were ignored by muting or temporary disables. It should be mentioned that if this particular CGF ignited it would destroy everything within a quarter mile and over pressure buildings up to a mile away.

On another site at the same facility. I encountered a lone operator at a sea water injection plant. He worked in a double hearing protection area and relied on auditory alarms emitted from a panel 150 feet from his station. Meaning he had foam ear plugs and over the head hearing protection. He could not hear the alarms and was at his wits end..

This is craziness. Double hearing protection and I can't hear a damn thing. I have to use hearing protection at work, but not double. The environment he works in alone sounds like enough to drown the alarm out.

I put out a fire in an electrical panel using a fire extinguisher and was a member of a volunteer fire brigade. I was stopped by an OHS inspector a few weeks later and asked what i would do if a fire broke out. I informed her that that situation had happened recently and i had dealt with it. She asked "have you been trained by the company to use extinguishers?" I said "no but i am a volunteer fire fighter." She told me i "should have notified the fire warden and not attempted to put the fire out." The companies fire training was to point an extinguisher at a pole pretending it was a fire and pretend to put it out. The fire brigade training was lighting a mix of diesel and kero floating on water in a large trough and using a real fire extinguisher to put it out.
